tagline: From the plaza to the ski basin, fifteen miles uphill.
intro: The byway starts at the Palace of the Governors on the Santa Fe Plaza and climbs east on NM 475 into the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, 15 miles through aspen and evergreen forest, with the Arroyo Seco badlands off in the distance. Past Hyde Memorial State Park it goes on to the Santa Fe Ski Basin, above 10,000 feet, and there the road simply ends.
Skiing came up here early. In 1936 the first rope tow in New Mexico went in at the future site of the basin, powered by the engine of a Packard sedan.

moments.title: Palace of the Governors
moments.text: The adobe seat of government from 1610, where territorial governor Lew Wallace wrote the last of Ben-Hur by a shaded lamp in 1879, fearing a bullet from outside.

moments.title: Hyde Memorial State Park
moments.text: Eight miles out of town the road jogs through the park past its massive stone-and-log lodge, and in winter people go tubing on its snowy hillsides.

moments.title: Ski Santa Fe
moments.text: The end of the road, near tree line, where chairlifts climb 1,650 vertical feet to Tesuque Peak at about 12,000 feet.
